prompt2:
This problem is a simplified version of Problem F.
You are given an integer sequence of length N: A = (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_N).
When splitting A at one position into two non-empty (contiguous) subarrays, find the maximum possible sum of the counts of distinct integers in those subarrays.
More formally, find the maximum sum of the following two values: the count of distinct integers in (A_1, A_2, \ldots, A_i), and the count of distinct integers in (A_{i+1}, A_{i+2}, \ldots, A_N).
Input
The input is given from Standard Input in the following format:
N
A_1 A_2 \ldots A_N
Output
Print the answer.
Constraints
- 2 \leq N \leq 3 \times 10^5
- 1 \leq A_i \leq N (1 \leq i \leq N)
- All input values are integers.

Clarification: Not explicitly covered by the given specification; a reasonable competitive-programming default applies, but this isn't the aspect actually left ambiguous here.

Clarification: The split is at a single position i, where 1 ≤ i ≤ N-1, ensuring both subarrays are non-empty.
